proposal.claim:
Origin, stated first. This is NOT from reports/SCOUT.jsonl, and the reason is a property of the evaluator rather than of the notebook. Of the thirteen payers now in it, most are anchored to a calendar or an announcement -- the quarterly delivery fixing over 07:00-08:00 UTC on the last Friday of a quarter, the Deribit expiry half-hour, the Dual Investment 07:30-08:00 fixing, the Monday 00:00 UTC liquidity-provider tier reset, the pre-announced margin-tier tightening, the BUSD wind-down, the delisting settlement -- and neither TrialConfig nor SignalTrialConfig has a field that can name a date, an hour, a weekday or an announcement. A Track A programme is anchored only to its own start offset, the evaluator enumerates every offset, and a 5th-percentile statistic taken across all of them averages a fixing hour away by construction. Five more -- forced short covering, short-gamma hedging, leveraged-token rebalancing, copy-trade replication and TWAP child orders -- need an intrabar forced-flow proxy, and H0008 and H0009 were both killed discovering that no such proxy exists in this vocabulary. One line, the venue-outage payer, says outright that its observable is the only one measurable entirely from the held panel, and it is right; but 'bars missing simultaneously across the cross-section' is a data-forensics measurement, not a rule any config field can express, and its honest home is a scout or robustness pass at zero ledger rows, not a registration. So the notebook is unreachable this pass, and this proposal says so plainly rather than borrowing an unreachable payer's language for a reachable rule -- which is exactly what killed H0008. The nearest notebook line is codex's liquidation-protocol payer: Binance removes the trader's discretion, submits an IOC order against the position, and charges a liquidation-clearance fee. This hypothesis stands on the paying side of that protocol and does not pretend to stand on the other. Track B is not proposed for a separate reason worth recording: its `rule` field admits only carry_funding and carry_funding_long, and both of those families are already closed, so Track B cannot be asked a new question until a new rule exists in the evaluator.

The new evidence, which did not exist before this pass. Two independent measurements now say the unlevered Track A accumulator is not merely taxed but RUINED, and no family on this track has ever asked about ruin. First, the adversary that killed H0011 measured, on funded weekly-ladder cells at leverage 1.0, liquidation_rate 0.430 on DOGEUSDT and 0.190 on ETHUSDT -- produced specifically to refute that proposal's assertion that nothing terminates early at leverage 1.0, and now on the record in configs/killed/H0011.json. Second, H0001's own surface reading records that near-break-even cells collapse to mwrr_q05 of EXACTLY -1.000 the moment include_funding is switched on: SOL +0.373 to -1.000, ETH +0.033 to -1.000, and ADA, DOGE, LTC and XRP all exactly -1.0. A metric pinned exactly at -1 is total loss of capital, which is the signature of ruin and not of a poor return. H0001 could not ask what prevents it, because H0001 fixed leverage at 1.0 -- and leverage is the only numeric Track A axis on which this project has never spent a single ledger row.

Who is structurally paying, and why they keep doing it. The perpetual long posts margin, and the venue charges rent against that same margin every eight hours, forever -- there is no date on which the contract stops owing, which is the whole product difference from a dated future. KT-1 measured the size of the bill (87% of BTCUSDT settlements positive, median 36% of contributed capital over three years); this asks who is charged when the bill outlives the buffer. The receivers are two, and that is the point. The funding counterparty collects the coupon; at the maintenance boundary the liquidation engine collects the fill and the insurance fund collects the residual, because the engine sells at market in whatever size happens to exist. The payer keeps standing there because the rent is levied on NOTIONAL while survival is set by MARGIN, and margin posted in excess of notional earns nothing at all -- so a holder who wants the exposure has a standing incentive to under-post, and the perpetual is the only continuously available levered long on this venue. That trade-off between the rent base and the survival base is not a knob; it is the rule shape, and it has never been varied here.

Why this is not a finer grid over H0001, and does not reopen KT-2. H0001 varied the deposit schedule and read a return; this holds the schedule fixed and varies the margin ratio, and its readout is liquidation_rate, a recorded metric that no Track A row has ever been read for. KT-2 is the precedent that leverage is a boundary coordinate and not a parameter -- it is one of the three established results and it is a leverage sweep -- and it covered 2x and above on a martingale that averages down. The interval (0, 1] on a plain ladder is unentered. No cell above 1.0 is proposed, so KT-2 is untouched. The value 0.25 is not exotic in this codebase: H0002's registered Track B grid already enumerated leverage 0.25.

Why the funding control is not a quantity the runner already records. The adversary's objection to H0011 was that its include_funding axis reconstructed funding_frac by tail-differenced subtraction of something the runner logs for free. That objection does not transfer. At leverage 1.0 price alone cannot bankrupt this account -- it would need a -100% move -- so L(1.0, false) is expected to be about zero, and L(1.0, true) minus L(1.0, false) is an EXACT attribution of ruin to the rent along a different simulated path, not a difference of two tails of the same one. No recorded quantity contains the unfunded liquidation path at any leverage, and none contains any path at leverage below 1.0. For the same reason this is not a question a script could answer off the ledger.

Design. contribution 100, stride_days 7, n_contributions 52 and hold_days 728: one year of weekly deposits, then two years of holding during which no fresh margin arrives. Total programme length is 1092 days on every cell -- KT-1's three-year frame, so funding_frac_q50 here is directly comparable with the 36% KT-1 measured. Every symbol in the universe has more pre-seal history than that (the shortest, DOGEUSDT, listed 2020-07), so there are no expected-NaN cells, unlike H0011. All eight configurations share one horizon by construction, so PBO is expected to be computable and tm_q05 is for once legitimately comparable within the grid; H0001's 'fewer than two configurations share a horizon' is designed out here rather than rediscovered. The universe is six: BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT and BNBUSDT, where H0011's adversary measured the low end of ruin, plus DOGEUSDT, XRPUSDT and ADAUSDT, three of the four symbols H0001's surface reading records collapsing to exactly -1.000. That spread is deliberate, because the family predicts that the required buffer orders with the size of the funding bill and therefore needs symbols at both ends of it.

What is honestly weak. Six symbols, and Track A independence comes from start dates over one history: H0001 reports between 1.02 and 1.40 independent paths per symbol on 1092-day cells, so this is at best six experiments and the report must say six. The best cell on the primary metric will be leverage 0.25 on every symbol whose 5th-percentile path is negative, which is arithmetic -- less exposure to a falling asset -- and is not a finding. Nothing in this shape can pay the accumulator: the best available outcome is a margin ratio that survives the rent, which is a map entry and not an edge. And this is a PARTIAL test of the named payer. The panel holds bars, not fills, so it can measure whether the ruin occurs and at what buffer it stops, but not what the ruin COST: the engine's actual fill, the clearance fee and any auto-deleveraging are outside this data entirely, and the report must not imply otherwise.
proposal.kill_condition:
Notation. Every cell is stride_days 7, n_contributions 52, hold_days 728 -- a total programme length of 1092 days. L(x, f) is the recorded liquidation_rate at leverage x with include_funding f; F(x) is funding_frac_q50 on the funded arm at leverage x. The universe is six symbols. The threshold 0.05 is frozen before any result is seen, and is chosen because the start-date ensemble carries roughly one independent path per symbol: below 5% of start offsets, ruin is one unlucky window rather than a property of the shape, and this data cannot tell those two apart.

Closed if the ruin is not there. If L(1.0, true) < 0.05 on 4 or more of the 6 symbols, the full-notional accumulator survives the rent, the 0.430 and 0.190 recorded in configs/killed/H0011.json belong to that proposal's cell shape and not to this one, and there is no boundary to map.

Closed also, even if that bar is cleared, if the rent is not what kills the account. Counting only symbols with L(1.0, true) >= 0.05: if L(1.0, false) >= 0.5 * L(1.0, true) on 3 or more of them, the account dies about as often with the funding leg switched off, the ruin is price and fees, and this family has named the wrong agent. If fewer than 3 symbols qualify to be counted, this clause is recorded as NOT EVALUABLE and may not be counted as survived.

Closed also if the buffer does not behave like a buffer. If L(x, true) is not non-increasing (ties allowed) along leverage 1.0 -> 0.75 -> 0.5 -> 0.25 on 2 or more of the 6 symbols, then cutting notional per dollar of margin does not monotonically reduce ruin, the mechanism is not margin, and no clause above may be read as one.

Closed also if the boundary lies outside the grid on the side of holding nothing. If L(0.25, true) > 0.05 on 4 or more of the 6 symbols, then no margin ratio at or above a quarter of notional survives the rent on this window. The family closes, and that sentence is the finding it records.

Closed also if the boundary does not track the bill. If the symbol with the largest F(1.0) is not among the three symbols with the largest L(1.0, true), then the buffer a symbol needs is not set by the rent it is charged, the family's cross-sectional prediction is wrong, and the survival map is being drawn by price drawdown -- a spot property that belongs to no perpetual-specific mechanism.

Closed also if the reported PBO is at or above 0.5 on a majority of the symbols for which it is computed. All eight configurations share one horizon by construction, so this clause is expected to be evaluable; if PBO comes back uncomputed on all six symbols, the report must record that this family's selection was never tested rather than counting this clause as survived.

Not counted toward any clause above. The primary metric's best cell is expected at leverage 0.25 wherever the 5th-percentile path is negative; neither its value nor its shape diagnostic is evidence for or against this family, and no cell of this grid may be presented anywhere as an accumulation rule worth running. The diagnostic is nevertheless computable here -- leverage carries four numeric levels, so the interior cells 0.5 and 0.75 each have a neighbour on both sides -- and if it reads PLATEAU rather than SPIKE that is worth recording and changes no clause.

verdict.reason: [claude] I ran the entire proposed 48-cell grid through run_trial in ~40 seconds with zero ledger rows, and five of the six kill clauses are already resolved to 'survives': L(1.0,true) = .570/.484/.000/.800/.724/.933 (clause 1 needs 4 below .05, gets 1), L(1.0,false) = 0.000 on all six (clause 2 can never fire), L(x,true) monotone on all 6 (clause 3), L(0.25,true)>.05 only on ADA (clause 4), and DOGE holds both the largest F(1.0)=3.557 and the 2nd-largest L (clause 5) — so registration buys a pre-determined outcome plus the section-6 right to enumerate 2000 cells next, for a map a zero-row script already draws. Compounding it: the rule shape is H0001's exactly (gate none, TP/SL null, unconditional weekly ladder) with two of its own numeric fields moved, the same criterion-4 defect that killed H0011 one pass earlier, and the 24 include_funding=false cells are pure padding — liquidation_rate 0.000 on every one and tm_q05 affine in leverage to under 2e-3, with funding_frac exactly proportional (3.000000000, 2.000000000). | [codex] This re-litigates the already-closed KT-1 perpetual-long DCA family and merely sweeps the leverage parameter of the same weekly accumulator; section 6 explicitly says an untried numeric axis is not a new rule shape. The liquidation-based kill conditions are concrete, but they do not justify permanently adding 48 rows for a finer grid over a closed mechanism.
